source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with myxedema has fatigue, cold intolerance, and facial puffiness. Lack of which hormones causes these findings?
questions.rationale: Myxedema results from inadequate thyroid hormone (T3 and T4), which lowers the basal metabolic rate and affects nearly every body system.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q64 (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: Myxedema results from inadequate thyroid hormone levels (T3 and T4).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Aling Cora, 34, is admitted with Graves' disease. She has weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, and an enlarged thyroid.
questions.stem: Which menstrual change should the nurse expect Aling Cora to report?
questions.rationale: Amenorrhea or decreased menstrual flow is common in Graves' disease (toxic diffuse goiter).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q65 (PDF p. 210)
questions.quote: Amenorrhea or a decreased menstrual flow is common in the client with Graves’ disease.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Aling Cora, 34, is admitted with Graves' disease. She has weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, and an enlarged thyroid.
questions.stem: Aling Cora will receive radioactive iodine. What should the nurse tell her?
options: It destroys the whole gland in one dose
Relief of symptoms may take 6 to 8 weeks
questions.rationale: Radioactive iodine lowers thyroid hormone levels over time. Symptom relief does not occur until about 6 to 8 weeks after treatment.
explanations: It reduces, not instantly destroys, the gland.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q253 (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: After treatment with radioactive iodine therapy, a decrease in the thyroid hormone level should be noted, which helps alleviate symptoms.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding in a client with acute pancreatitis shows paralytic ileus has developed?
options: A firm mass at the right costal margin
questions.rationale: Inflammation such as pancreatitis can cause paralytic ileus, a nonmechanical obstruction. Inability to pass flatus is a sign.
explanations: Correct: a sign of paralytic ileus.
Pain in ileus is more diffuse.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q181 (PDF p. 334)
questions.quote: Inability to pass flatus is a clinical manifestation of paralytic ileus.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Mang Ponso, 60, a heavy drinker for 30 years, is admitted with cirrhosis and massive ascites.
questions.stem: Mang Ponso is short of breath from the ascites. What is the PRIORITY nursing measure?
options: Raise the head of the bed
questions.rationale: Ascitic fluid pushes up on the diaphragm. Raising the head of the bed uses gravity to relieve the pressure and ease breathing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q202 (PDF p. 356)
questions.quote: Elevating the head of the bed enlists the aid of gravity in relieving pressure on the diaphragm.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Mang Ponso, 60, a heavy drinker for 30 years, is admitted with cirrhosis and massive ascites.
questions.stem: Which diet does the nurse expect for Mang Ponso?
questions.rationale: With ascites, sodium and possibly fluids are restricted. Fat stays normal, carbohydrates are sufficient, and calories are 2,000 to 3,000 a day.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q621 (PDF p. 836)
questions.quote: If the client has ascites, sodium and possibly fluids would be restricted in the diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Mang Ponso, 60, a heavy drinker for 30 years, is admitted with cirrhosis and massive ascites.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Ponso at discharge shows he needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is avoided in cirrhosis because it can cause fatal liver damage. Rest, nutrition, and weight monitoring are appropriate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q641 (PDF p. 859)
questions.quote: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is avoided because it can cause fatal liver damage in the client with cirrhosis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Ate Rose, 42, has a subtotal thyroidectomy for a large goiter.
questions.stem: Which item should be at Ate Rose's bedside after surgery?
questions.rationale: Swelling in the tracheal area after thyroidectomy can cause respiratory distress, so an emergency tracheostomy kit is kept at the bedside, along with oxygen and suction.
explanations: Thyroid surgery does not alter heat control.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q259 (PDF p. 416)
questions.quote: Respiratory distress can occur after thyroidectomy as a result of swelling in the tracheal area.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Ate Rose, 42, has a subtotal thyroidectomy for a large goiter.
questions.stem: Which finding suggests the parathyroid glands were damaged during Ate Rose's surgery?
questions.rationale: Parathyroid damage lowers PTH, causing hypocalcemia and tetany. Tingling around the mouth or of the fingers and toes, and muscle twitching, are early signs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q372 (PDF p. 540)
questions.quote: Hypocalcemia and tetany result when parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels decrease.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Ate Rose, 42, has a subtotal thyroidectomy for a large goiter.
questions.stem: Which statement by Ate Rose before surgery shows she understands the teaching?
options: 'I'll support my neck when I cough or move.'
'I should keep my head bent forward.'
'I can turn my head freely right away.'
questions.rationale: Supporting the neck when coughing or moving reduces tension on the incision. Removing the thyroid does not mean taking antithyroid drugs afterward.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q759 (PDF p. 988)
questions.quote: One way of reducing incisional tension is to teach the client how to support the neck when coughing or being repositioned.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which assessment gives the BEST data about hypothyroidism on admission?
questions.rationale: Inspecting the face reveals coarse features, puffiness around the eyes, and the blank expression typical of hypothyroidism.
explanations: The thyroid is palpated, not percussed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q301 (PDF p. 464)
questions.quote: Inspection of facial features will reveal the characteristic coarse features, presence of edema around the eyes and face

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding does the nurse expect in a client with hypothyroidism?
questions.rationale: Low thyroid hormone slows metabolism: bradycardia, hypotension, cool dry scaly skin, low body temperature, brittle hair, and cold intolerance.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q383 (PDF p. 552)
questions.quote: Some of these manifestations are bradycardia; hypotension; cool, dry, scaly skin; decreased body temperature

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After transsphenoidal pituitary surgery, which assessment detects a common temporary complication?
questions.rationale: Surgical trauma can cause temporary diabetes insipidus from ADH deficiency, with polyuria of 4 to 24 L a day. Urine output and weight are monitored.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q335 (PDF p. 503)
questions.quote: A common complication of surgery on the pituitary gland is temporary diabetes insipidus.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding should the nurse plan to manage in a client with diabetes insipidus?
questions.rationale: ADH deficiency causes massive urine output, poor skin turgor, dry mucous membranes, narrowed pulse pressure, tachycardia, and hypotension.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q384 (PDF p. 553)
questions.quote: Clinical manifestations include poor skin turgor, increased urinary output, dry mucous membranes, decreased pulse pressure

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which intervention belongs in the post-hypophysectomy care plan?
questions.rationale: Diabetes insipidus or SIADH can develop, so daily weights and I&O are monitored. The head of the bed is raised. Coughing and toothbrushing are avoided because they can disrupt the surgical site and cause a CSF leak.
explanations: Coughing raises ICP and strains the site.
Avoided to protect the surgical site.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q371 (PDF p. 539)
questions.quote: obtaining daily weights and monitoring intake and output are important interventions.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Discharge teaching after a UNILATERAL adrenalectomy should include:
options: Taking steroids that will be tapered off
questions.rationale: After removal of one adrenal gland, corticosteroids are given temporarily and tapered off; lifelong replacement is not needed. Steroids also mask infection, so the client watches for its signs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q337 (PDF p. 505)
questions.quote: will be placed on corticosteroids temporarily to avoid a cortisol deficiency; lifelong replacement is not necessary.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which question BEST elicits data about hyperparathyroidism?
options: 'Do you have joint or bone pain?'
questions.rationale: Excess PTH pulls calcium from bone, causing demineralization and bone and joint pain, along with hypercalcemia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q379 (PDF p. 548)
questions.quote: When bone reabsorption is increased, calcium is released from the bones into the blood, causing hypercalcemia.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which item MUST be at the bedside after a parathyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage and swelling can compress the trachea and cause respiratory distress, so a tracheotomy set is routinely placed at the bedside.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q547 (PDF p. 748)
questions.quote: An emergency tracheotomy set is always routinely placed at the bedside of the client with this type of surgery

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The cause of a client's acute abdominal pain is not yet known. Which order should the nurse question?
questions.rationale: Until the cause is known and the need for surgery is decided, the client is kept NPO with an IV line. A clear liquid diet would be questioned.
explanations: Correct: the client should be NPO.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q419 (PDF p. 596)
questions.quote: the nurse would question a prescription to give a clear liquid diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with type 1 diabetes about sick days needs correction?
options: 'I'll stop my insulin if I'm vomiting.'
'I'll call my doctor if ill more than 24 hours.'
'I'll check my sugar every 2 to 4 hours.'
questions.rationale: Insulin is continued even when vomiting and unable to eat, to prevent DKA. Blood glucose is checked every 2 to 4 hours during illness.
explanations: Correct answer: stopping insulin risks DKA.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q631 (PDF p. 848)
questions.quote: The client needs to be instructed to take insulin, even if he or she is vomiting and unable to eat.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement about hypoglycemia shows a client needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll take extra insulin if I feel shaky.'
questions.rationale: Insulin lowers blood glucose further and is never a treatment for hypoglycemia. The client takes 10 to 15 g of simple carbohydrate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q632 (PDF p. 850)
questions.quote: Insulin is not taken as a treatment for hypoglycemia because the insulin will lower the blood glucose level.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which food should a client recovering from pancreatitis AVOID?
questions.rationale: Spicy foods, alcohol, coffee, tea, and heavy meals stimulate pancreatic secretions and can trigger attacks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q640 (PDF p. 858)
questions.quote: The client must avoid spicy foods such as chili, alcohol, coffee, tea, and heavy meals

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client is discharged after hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS). Which teaching is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Dehydration in HHS can be severe and progress rapidly, so reporting its signs is the priority.
explanations: Part of teaching, not the priority.
Part of teaching, not the priority.
Part of teaching, not the priority.
Correct: dehydration is the main danger.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q686 (PDF p. 907)
questions.quote: Clients at risk for HHS should report signs and symptoms of dehydration to primary health care providers.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When planning diabetes care for an older client, what should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Encourage family to do her care
questions.rationale: The nurse first assesses self-care ability. Planning menus and relying on others promote dependence, and hands-on practice works better than video.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q687 (PDF p. 908)
questions.quote: The nurse first assesses the client’s ability for self-care.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with gastritis asks which pain reliever will not upset the stomach. The nurse recommends:
questions.rationale: Aspirin and NSAIDs such as naproxen and ibuprofen irritate the GI tract. Acetaminophen does not.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q717 (PDF p. 939)
questions.quote: The client should be advised to take analgesics that do not contain aspirin, such as acetaminophen.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with Cushing's syndrome understands discharge teaching?
options: 'I'll check my stools for dark color.'
'I'll stop steroids suddenly if I feel well.'
questions.rationale: Excess cortisol increases gastric acid, which can cause peptic ulcers and GI bleeding, so stool color is checked. Potassium-rich foods are encouraged because hypokalemia occurs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q754 (PDF p. 983)
questions.quote: Cortisol stimulates the secretion of gastric acid, and this can result in the development of peptic ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with type 1 diabetes has a glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) of 10%. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Good control in the past week
Poor glucose control over recent weeks
questions.rationale: HbA1c reflects glucose control over the previous 6 to 8 weeks and is not affected by diet in the last day or two. A level of 10% shows poor control.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q757 (PDF p. 986)
questions.quote: Glycosylated hemoglobin is a measure of glucose control during the 6 to 8 weeks before the test.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When is hypoglycemia MOST likely after an insulin injection?
options: At the end of its duration
questions.rationale: Reactions are most likely at peak time, when the insulin is at its maximum action. Regular insulin peaks in about 2 hours; NPH in 4 to 12 hours.
explanations: Risk is highest at the peak.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q758 (PDF p. 987)
questions.quote: Insulin reactions are most likely to occur during the peak time after insulin administration

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which instruction helps a client with type 1 diabetes manage the risk of hypoglycemia?
questions.rationale: Glucose tablets treat a hypoglycemic reaction. Glucagon may be prescribed if the client becomes unconscious and cannot swallow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q765 (PDF p. 994)
questions.quote: Glucose tablets are taken if a hypoglycemic reaction occurs.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with peptic ulcer disease shows effective teaching?
options: 'I'll take antacids with my H2 blocker.'
questions.rationale: Eating slowly and chewing well prevent overdistention and reflux. Bedtime snacks raise night acid, aspirin and NSAIDs are avoided, and antacids interfere with H2 blockers.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q781 (PDF p. 1011)
questions.quote: Eating slowly and chewing thoroughly helps prevent overdistention and reflux.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which dietary statement by a client with GERD needs correction?
questions.rationale: Fluids are taken between meals to prevent overdistention and reflux. Coffee, tea, cola, and chocolate lower LES pressure.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q783 (PDF p. 1013)
questions.quote: Fluids must be taken between meals rather than with meals to prevent the overdistention that leads to reflux.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with a colostomy complains of odor. Which food helps reduce it?
questions.rationale: Yogurt, buttermilk, cranberry juice, and parsley help reduce odor. Eggs, fish, onions, cucumbers, mushrooms, and cabbage cause odor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q791 (PDF p. 1021)
questions.quote: Foods that help eliminate odor with a colostomy include yogurt, buttermilk, cranberry juice, and parsley.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: For a client newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, which teaching is MOST important initially?
questions.rationale: Before teaching self-management, the client must understand the disease itself. Diet, glucose testing, and insulin technique follow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q811 (PDF p. 1045)
questions.quote: Before educating about a disease process, it is important that the client understands the components of the disease process.
